reason: Conversation 1 reached a sensible diagnosis in three turns: a radiant element is the most likely cause, with a faulty control module or loose wiring as less likely alternatives. It then escalated to an engineer without suggesting any dismantling and without naming an unsupported part. It was a little muddled early on (child lock, induction), but it stayed safe and well calibrated. Conversation 2 opened with an irrelevant House of Blues answer. It suggested removing the glass top and resetting at the breaker, which is unsafe given the homeowner's refusal. It kept pointing the homeowner to a sticker under the glass and then repeatedly truncated its replies, so the model number question was never answered. It also left the user without a clear escalation path to an engineer.
